editorial:
Imagine you lose your favorite dog, and the only way to find out what happened is by watching old home videos and listening to secret voice notes. That is exactly what you get in this creepy mystery. You follow a filmmaker who is desperate to find his dog, Latte, but as he puts the footage together, the vibe shifts from a sad search to something way more scary. The way the movie uses found footage makes you feel like you are solving the puzzle right along with him, and the weird behavior of the local cats adds a layer of tension that keeps you on edge.

What really works here is the slow build-up to the big reveal. The acting feels real, and the pacing is just right so you do not get bored. While some parts might feel a bit slow at first, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love stories that make you question what is real, you need to see this. For the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the background, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that the dog who returned is not actually Latte. The neighborhood cats are actually part of a strange hive mind that replaced the real dog with a fake, skin-walking creature. The final scene shows the filmmaker realizing the dog in his house is an impostor when it starts acting human. It ends with the creature staring into the camera, leaving you wondering if the whole neighborhood has been replaced.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and weird twists.
